meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 6: Client Best Practices
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A host connects to servers exposing 400 tools, and the definitions crowd the model's context. Which pattern does the guidance recommend?

options.text: Load every definition once at the start of the session and cache them in the system prompt
Progressive discovery: a light catalog, full schemas for candidates, then the call
Ask the model to call tools/list itself whenever it needs a tool
Limit the host to one server at a time so the catalog stays small

questions.explanation: The Catalog to Inspect to Execute loop keeps a light list in context, fetches full schemas only for likely candidates, then executes, with keyword, embedding or sub-agent search to pick candidates. The client refreshes on notifications/tools/list_changed.

questions.question: A client treats ttlMs as a polling interval and re-fetches tools/list every time it expires. What does the spec say?

options.text: That is correct behaviour, and the reason servers are required to send ttlMs
Polling is fine as long as the interval is at least the value of ttlMs
Don't: TTL is a freshness hint checked on access; pollers MUST use jitter and backoff
Polling is fine whenever the server did not advertise listChanged in its declared capabilities

questions.explanation: Clients SHOULD NOT treat TTL as a polling trigger: they check freshness when they need the data and re-fetch only if stale. Implementations that do poll MUST apply jitter and backoff.

questions.question: Two connected servers both expose a tool called search. What should your client do before showing them to the model?

options.text: Drop the second one, since duplicate tool names are a protocol violation
Ask each server to rename its tool through a tools/update request
Merge them into one entry and pick a server at call time by round-robin
Qualify each name with its server so the model can tell the two apart

questions.explanation: Tool names are unique only within one server, so a client that pools several servers must namespace them and keep the mapping back to the right connection. Dropping or merging silently sends calls to the wrong backend, and there is no tools/update method.

questions.question: Your client sends a progressToken and puts a progress bar on screen. What must it be built to tolerate?

options.text: That no progress notification ever arrives, because sending them is optional
That progress arrives exactly once, immediately before the result
That progress notifications replace the result entirely when the work runs long
That the server rejects the request if it cannot report progress

questions.explanation: A progressToken is an invitation, not a contract: a conformant server may send many notifications, or none at all, and must still return the result normally. A UI that stalls without progress updates is a client bug.

questions.question: A tool returns a 200 KB JSON blob and it swamps the model's context. Which handling does the client guidance favour?

options.text: Feed the whole result in, since omitting any of it risks a wrong answer
Reject results above a fixed size and report a tool error to the user
Split the result across several turns so the model eventually sees all of it
Summarise or truncate for the model while keeping a reference to the full result

questions.explanation: The client owns what enters context and is expected to manage it, passing the model what it needs while keeping the full payload retrievable. Discarding results or paging an entire blob through the conversation wastes context without improving answers.

questions.question: Why should servers return tools in a deterministic order, and what should clients avoid?

options.text: Stable order preserves client caches and LLM prompt caches; avoid re-sorting mid-conversation
Stable order guarantees stable tool ids; avoid renaming tools between calls
Stable order lets clients diff lists cheaply; avoid caching any list for longer than its advertised TTL
Stable order is required by the schema; avoid returning more than 100 tools

questions.explanation: Deterministic ordering lets clients cache the list reliably and improves prompt-cache hit rates when tools sit in the model's context. Clients should append new definitions after the cache breakpoint rather than re-sorting, or route calls through one stable meta-tool.

questions.question: In code mode, the model writes a script that calls tools. Which property does the guidance require of that sandbox?

options.text: Full network access, so the script can reach the same APIs the tools use
One blanket approval per script, covering every call the script makes
No network access: every call goes through the host broker, which holds the credentials
Credentials injected as environment variables, so the script can authenticate directly

questions.explanation: The sandbox has no network of its own and every tool call is brokered by the host, so credentials never reach generated code. Authorization stays per call: approving a script is not a blanket approval, and isError results surface as exceptions.
